name: sgl-router POLICY_DESIGN.md target design (per-engine admission limits, bucket fallback, error mapping)
notes: Explicitly a TARGET design, not a specification of the current API or CLI: 'It defines responsibilities and behavior; the interface and configuration examples are sketches, not a specification of the current API or CLI. Implementation status is listed at the end.' Recorded as contested for exactly that reason. Substantive content: AdmissionLimits caps map to engine metrics - max_running_requests (reported running requests), max_waiting_requests (reported waiting requests), max_kv_tokens (reported total KV tokens), max_pending_prefill_tokens (reported waiting uncached tokens), max_inflight_requests (router-local in-flight requests). 'Limits are absolute caps; they do not default to capacities reported by the engine. Unknown fields are rejected during deserialization.' Critically: 'Request size is not part of admission: buckets already select by input length and context capacity, and admission only observes load without reserving it' - a documented admission race. 'Reported metrics are None without a fresh, complete report, never zero, and such limits fail open; the in-flight count is always known.' Error mapping: an empty bucket list becomes a 400 NoMatchingBucket response; exhausting the list with accumulated admission rejections produces a 503 selection failure; with no admission rejections the last unavailable stage produces a stage-specific 503; InvalidSignal, InvalidConfiguration and OutsideCandidates stop the pass with an internal error; successful selection ends the pass and forwarding errors do not restart bucket iteration.
